Aquatic

/uh-KWAT-ik/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Aquatic means living or growing in water, or relating to water.

Aquatic means living or growing in water, or relating to water. Mayfly nymphs are entirely aquatic, breathing through feathery gills for a year before their single day in the air.

Worked Example

A stream survey lifts one flat stone and finds three animals beneath it. A caddisfly larva in a case of glued sand grains breathes through gills and dies within minutes in the open air. A diving beetle carries a bubble of air under its wing cases, but it hunts, mates, and lays its eggs below the surface. A stonefly nymph clings to the stone's underside and will not leave the water until the day it becomes a winged adult. All three are aquatic animals.

All three creatures feed, breathe, and breed in the stream itself and cannot live out of it, which is what aquatic means.

How Aquatic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

water-dwelling

water-dwelling: living in water

marine

marine: living in the sea

Antonyms

land-dwelling

land-dwelling: living on dry land

airborne

airborne: carried or living in the air

How Strong Is It? — water-loving → aquatic → submerged

water-loving vs. aquatic

water-loving vs. aquatic: Water-loving describes anything that thrives near water, including a plant rooted on a wet bank, while aquatic means living in the water itself.

submerged vs. aquatic

submerged vs. aquatic: Submerged is stronger and more literal, since an aquatic plant may lift its flowers into the air while a submerged one is under water entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — aqua-

Root — aqua-: water (Latin aqua)

Suffix — -tic

Suffix — -tic: relating to; of the nature of

Put it together

Put it together: Latin aqua meant water, plainly and simply, and it has poured into English almost unchanged. An aquarium is a water-place, an aqueduct leads water across a valley, and an aquifer carries it underground. Aquatic keeps the root at its most general: belonging to the water.

Use the root in a new word: aquifer

Use the root in a new word: aquifer: An aquifer is a rock layer that carries water underground, from aqua ('water') and ferre ('to carry'), sharing its first half with aquatic.

Root Check

Word Choice

scientific and everyday

Aquatic covers fresh water and salt water alike, while marine narrows the idea to the sea. Its land-side counterpart in this unit is terrestrial, and creatures that genuinely split their lives between the two, such as frogs and newts, are called amphibious rather than either one.
